notes:
I checked all 49 claims against the worktree at 62551b06 and found 6 that do not match the code: K7a-092, -296, -297, -298, -317 and -333. All are in longitudinal_aircraft.md sections 3 and 4.

How I ran the probes: test/Project.toml in the worktree has no RedstoneExamples, so I ran them with --project=examples/test instead. The scripts check that both packages load from the worktree; out.txt shows they do. The files are probe.jl and probe2.jl in /Users/miguel/.julia/dev/Redstone.jl/design/reports/20261124_doc_conformance/probes/K7a_v/, with output in out.txt and out2.txt. probe.jl defines closed_loop_Tt, a copy of closed_loop with every Tt set from an argument, by evaluating edited source text inside RedstoneExamples. Nothing tracked was changed.

The most substantive finding is K7a-298. The DiscretePID correction uses the exact step β = 1 − e^(−Δt/Tt), so at Tt equal to one period it closes 63% of the gap per tick, not all of it. The closed_loop docstring at examples/src/longitudinal.jl:435-436 makes the same claim. I classed it drift because pid_anti_windup.md records the exact step. Strictly it was never a move: the exact step predates this companion.

Left open:
- K7a-296 and -297 depend on how 'during it' and 'whatever Tt is' are read, so their fixes are marked not clear.
- K7a-120: autopilot's root also holds a Constant `engaged` beside the groups. I left it as conforming.
- The 'about 4 rad/s' slew in K7a-341's sentence was not probed with a window that excludes the step.
